subject: physics
title: Astrophysics Adventure 2: HR diagram and stellar evolution
welcome_lead: Today you'll plot stars on the HR diagram and follow them from birth to death.
meta_desc: Physics — HR diagram, main sequence, giants, white dwarfs, stellar evolution.
final_note: You learned HR diagram plots L vs T (or M vs spectral class); main sequence holds 90% of stars; massive stars end as black holes, low mass as white dwarfs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Plot L (or M) on y-axis vs T (or spectral class O B A F G K M) on x-axis (x reversed: hot left).

Most stars (90%) sit on the main sequence, running diagonally from hot-bright (top-left) to cool-dim (bottom-right).

Off-MS: red giants (top-right), white dwarfs (bottom-left).

Nebula → gravity collapses → protostar → fusion ignites → main sequence.

Sun on MS for ~10 Gyr (born 4.6 Gyr ago, ~5 Gyr remain).

After H exhausted: shell burning → red giant (Sun will engulf Earth).

Low mass (≤ 8 M_⊙): planetary nebula + white dwarf (C/O core, Earth-sized).

High mass (≥ 8 M_⊙): supernova → neutron star or black hole.

Chandrasekhar limit ~1.4 M_⊙ for WD; ~2-3 M_⊙ for neutron star.

Crab Nebula (supernova 1054 AD recorded by Chinese astronomers) — global perspective on astronomy.
